analysis.title: Nvidia's Steve Jobs moment: the next big test for the AI king
key_insights: The Market Ear's Sept 23 AAPL/NVDA relative trade (AAPL calls vs NVDA puts) has delivered, and the AAPL/NVDA gap has widened sharply since, accelerated by the latest Huang news. The thesis was that Nvidia need not lose existing orders for the relative narrative to shift, because AI inference moving onto devices and local machines could leave Nvidia with a smaller share of incremental AI demand than the market expects.

On Sept 23 Goldman flagged NVDA implied volatility at its lowest since before COVID while the stock traded near range highs. The setup favored puts, since a shift in the AI inference narrative could hit the stock before earnings estimates moved. The Market Ear says that if you still hold the AAPL calls vs NVDA puts trade, it is time to close it and move on.

At today's lows NVDA was down nearly 40% from its early-October all-time highs, approaching the Liberation Day drawdown earlier this year, which exceeded 40% but unfolded at a much slower pace. NVDA also traded nearly 30% below its 200-day moving average at the lows, matching the undershoot seen in the Liberation Day panic.

Goldman's Jim Schneider compares Nvidia now to Apple during Steve Jobs' 2011 departure. Apple's forward P/E compressed from 17x to 12x and bottomed near 9x in 2013 before recovering as investors gained confidence in management's execution without Jobs. Schneider expects a similar period of multiple uncertainty for Nvidia until leadership and business momentum are clearer.

Goldman forecasts roughly 80% EPS growth for Nvidia, and Schneider sees attractive risk/reward at current levels. The open question is whether Nvidia can show, as Apple did, that the business is bigger than its iconic leader.
